bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical risk in overseas markets — With projects spanning 20+ countries, political instability or sudden changes in certain geographies can disrupt execution and supply chains; the war-like situation in the Middle East already led the Company to postpone its planned equity investment in UAE subsidiary Transrail Trading LLC and delay use of IPO proceeds.
- Reduction in order intake — A slowdown in infrastructure investment can lower order inflows and revenue; the Company relies on Power T&D prioritisation, its global presence and diversification into Railways, Civil, Solar EPC and Poles & Lighting to cushion regional slowdowns.
- Commodity price variation — Fluctuations in steel, aluminium, zinc and cement can erode profitability, particularly under fixed-price contracts; mitigated through escalation clauses, commodity forward contracts or back-to-back firm-price vendor agreements, and contingencies where hedging is not feasible.
- Execution risk — Manpower shortages, difficult terrain, Right of Way dependencies and delays in regulatory approvals and clearances can hinder project timelines on large turnkey EPC projects.
- Foreign currency fluctuation — Operating across multiple countries exposes the Company to exchange-rate volatility; international tenders are typically quoted in USD/EUR and onshore portions in local currency to maintain a natural hedge.
- Interest rate fluctuation — Volatility in interest rates can adversely affect profitability; borrowing levels are reviewed to reduce working-capital intensity.
- Environment, health & safety — EHS incidents can endanger employees and workers on project sites; managed through onsite safety officers, corporate safety audits and a monthly EHS Steering Committee.
- Succession planning — Insufficient planning for leadership transitions at key positions can threaten long-term organisational stability; addressed via annual identification of critical roles and periodic succession-plan reviews.

Tower manufacturing capacity was doubled from 84,000 MTPA to 172,400 MTPA, including the Phase 1 brownfield expansion of the existing Deoli tower plant and the greenfield Butibori (Nagpur) tower plant, whose commissioning the Corporate Overview dates to April 2026; tower capacity is to rise further to 196,000 MTPA in FY 2026-27. Phase 2 brownfield expansions for both towers and conductors are expected to be completed by Q2 FY27. outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Government of India has outlined a transmission investment opportunity of approximately Rs 9.15 lakh crore through 2032 for new corridors, network augmentation and advanced transmission technologies.
- Domestic transmission ordering witnessed a temporary slowdown in FY26, with fewer schemes awarded than the previous year, attributed primarily to execution constraints rather than demand weakness.
- HVDC projects are expected to drive future growth, with a steady pipeline of project awards anticipated in the coming years.
- ISTS pipeline as of 31 March 2026: 25 transmission schemes under bidding, 230 under construction and 14 under approval.
- Global drivers of grid investment: rising electricity demand, renewable integration, modernisation of ageing networks, EV adoption, data centres and energy-security concerns; over 2,500 GW of projects stalled in connection queues makes transmission the bottleneck of the energy transition.
- Africa: large electricity access gap (more than 600 million people without reliable supply) and multilateral programmes (SDG 7, M300) create a durable pipeline for transmission and grid infrastructure.
- Middle East: electricity demand growing nearly 4% annually, oil-to-gas switching and solar scaling support grid investment across the Gulf.
- US: electricity consumption projected to grow nearly 2% annually through 2030, driven by data centres and AI infrastructure.
- The outbreak of war in the Middle East in late February 2026 interrupted the improving global economic trajectory, creating near-term uncertainty.
- Domestic Power T&D unexecuted order book of Rs 8,841 crore as on March 31, 2026, after orders secured mainly involving many 765 kV transmission lines.
- International unexecuted order book of Rs 6,225 crore, with new orders from Tanzania, Djibouti, Tunisia, Abu Dhabi and Mozambique.
- Civil Construction year-end unexecuted order book of Rs 790 crore after 4 jobs secured during the year.
- Railways' share of the unexecuted order book continues to be just 2%.
- Management states the closing order book keeps it assured that the growth momentum will broadly continue.

risks.note: With projects spanning 20+ countries, political instability or sudden changes in certain geographies can disrupt execution and supply chains; the war-like situation in the Middle East already led the Company to postpone its planned equity investment in UAE subsidiary Transrail Trading LLC and delay use of IPO proceeds.

A slowdown in infrastructure investment can lower order inflows and revenue; the Company relies on Power T&D prioritisation, its global presence and diversification into Railways, Civil, Solar EPC and Poles & Lighting to cushion regional slowdowns.

Fluctuations in steel, aluminium, zinc and cement can erode profitability, particularly under fixed-price contracts; mitigated through escalation clauses, commodity forward contracts or back-to-back firm-price vendor agreements, and contingencies where hedging is not feasible.
Manpower shortages, difficult terrain, Right of Way dependencies and delays in regulatory approvals and clearances can hinder project timelines on large turnkey EPC projects.

Operating across multiple countries exposes the Company to exchange-rate volatility; international tenders are typically quoted in USD/EUR and onshore portions in local currency to maintain a natural hedge.
Volatility in interest rates can adversely affect profitability; borrowing levels are reviewed to reduce working-capital intensity.
EHS incidents can endanger employees and workers on project sites; managed through onsite safety officers, corporate safety audits and a monthly EHS Steering Committee.

Insufficient planning for leadership transitions at key positions can threaten long-term organisational stability; addressed via annual identification of critical roles and periodic succession-plan reviews.

- Unexecuted order book INR 16,361 cr (incl. L1), up from 14,551 cr → >2 years revenue visibility.

- Power T&D ~90% of revenue; substations <5% (smaller part).

- During FY26: completed seven 765 kV transmission projects in India; supplied >1,50,000 MT towers, 4,000 km conductors; entered Abu Dhabi, Tunisia, Djibouti, Botswana.
6 growth verticals / optionality:
- HVDC projects upcoming — part of multi-year cycle (>2,00,000 km lines to be added; >INR 9,00,000 cr investment outlook over 5 years).

- Multilateral-development-bank-funded international projects (preferred for risk management).
- Construction-productivity capex (new INR 203 cr) to improve execution speed.
7 margins & cost dynamics:
- FY26 margin 11.92% within guided 11.5-12%; FY25 was 12.7% (mgmt insists not apples-to-apples — project mix/geography driven).
- Q4 RM cost % rose sharply on commodity inflation + March supply-chain disruption.
- ~30-35% of contracts have price-variation (pass-through) clauses; rest fixed → margin exposure to commodity inflation.
- Finance cost ~INR 210-220 cr; LC discounting + interest blended 8.5-9% (LC charges ~INR 40-50 cr); expects 50-100 bps reduction next year.
- Claims best/one-of-best margin profile in T&D industry.
8 capex / expansion:
- IPO Phase-1 (~INR 520 cr Phase 1+2) completing by Q2 FY27: tower capacity 1,72,000 → 1,96,000 MTPA (more than doubled vs pre-expansion); conductor 24,000 → 49,500 km (doubling) by Q2/Q3 FY27.

- Butibori greenfield + brownfield expansion.
9 capital allocation:
- Net debt cut 30% to INR 274 cr (INR 181 cr ex-IPO funds); OCF doubled (~INR 816 cr from 415 cr).
- WC days 81 (from 91), targeting sub-80; finance-cost/revenue improved 55 bps.
- Trade acceptances ~INR 1,200 cr — to stay broadly flat; uses RXIL/VFS for credit.
- 100% dividend (INR 2/sh); ROCE 25.79% (>24% for 3yrs).
10 risks & watch-items:
- Geopolitical / supply-chain disruption (Feb-Mar) deferring execution & inflating costs (fuel, shipping, insurance) — primary reason for pruned FY27 guidance.
- Order-inflow miss (INR 8,520 cr vs ~10,000 cr target) — slippage risk into Q1 FY27.
- Lumpy quarterly revenue (project lifecycle) — Q4 de-growth; not to be read QoQ.
- Labour demand-supply tightness (managed via training/loyalty programs).
- Right-of-way / forest / statutory clearance delays (client-side; covered by EOT).
- Rising competition from road-EPC entrants into T&D (mgmt won't chase volume at lower margin).

Emphasizes "fair and prudent" guidance, selective bidding, risk-managed (MDB-funded preference). Deflects QoQ scrutiny toward annual numbers; transparent on order-inflow miss and tax/finance-cost queries (some bookkeeping items deferred to IR). 42-year operating history cited repeatedly.
12 non-obvious takeaways:
- Q4 weakness is structural to project cycle (20 projects closed in Dec = high-margin closures front-loaded into H1), NOT demand loss — revenue "deferred not lost."
- The ~11% margin guide bakes in commodity inflation AND the fact only ~35% of book has pass-through; upside is real if supply chain normalizes.
- New INR 203 cr capex is construction-equipment-led — a tell that execution productivity (not capacity) is now the binding constraint on the 20-25% growth ambition.
- Backward integration (own conductors/towers, full PQs) is the moat vs road-EPC new entrants.
- SEB/TBCB is a large untapped optionality (~20% of pipeline) management is deliberately under-exposed to.

- Government of India has outlined a transmission investment opportunity of approximately Rs 9.15 lakh crore through 2032 for new corridors, network augmentation and advanced transmission technologies.

- ISTS pipeline as of 31 March 2026: 25 transmission schemes under bidding, 230 under construction and 14 under approval.
- Global drivers of grid investment: rising electricity demand, renewable integration, modernisation of ageing networks, EV adoption, data centres and energy-security concerns; over 2,500 GW of projects stalled in connection queues makes transmission the bottleneck of the energy transition.
- Africa: large electricity access gap (more than 600 million people without reliable supply) and multilateral programmes (SDG 7, M300) create a durable pipeline for transmission and grid infrastructure.
- Middle East: electricity demand growing nearly 4% annually, oil-to-gas switching and solar scaling support grid investment across the Gulf.
- US: electricity consumption projected to grow nearly 2% annually through 2030, driven by data centres and AI infrastructure.
- The outbreak of war in the Middle East in late February 2026 interrupted the improving global economic trajectory, creating near-term uncertainty.
- Domestic Power T&D unexecuted order book of Rs 8,841 crore as on March 31, 2026, after orders secured mainly involving many 765 kV transmission lines.
- International unexecuted order book of Rs 6,225 crore, with new orders from Tanzania, Djibouti, Tunisia, Abu Dhabi and Mozambique.
- Civil Construction year-end unexecuted order book of Rs 790 crore after 4 jobs secured during the year.
- Railways' share of the unexecuted order book continues to be just 2%.
